transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-11-11 14:00 UTC | Duration: 42m | Attendees: Samira (Redwood AE), Daniel (Redwood SE), Lina (AurumTech Head of AI), Marcus (Infra Lead), Priya (Security)

[00:00] Samira: Hey everyone thanks for joining, I'm Samira from Redwood inference, I'll kick us off. we had Lina requested a dedicated capacity discussion so we can focus on isolation and burst behavior.
[00:28] Lina: Thanks Samira, yeah we want to understand committed GPU pricing, whether Redwood Dedicated gives us the isolation we need and how bursting works — we expect spiky demand at month end.
[00:45] Daniel: Hi all, Daniel here, I'm the SE. quick agenda: workload profile, current infra, security requirements, and then capacity/scale recommendations and pilot.
[01:12] Marcus: For context, our stack today runs inference on a mix of in‑house GPU boxes and some cloud instances. we do online completions and batch embeddings, about 10M tokens/day average, peaks up to 3x. latency SLO around 200ms tail for core flows.
[01:38] Priya: From security we're SOC2 in progress, we need KMS integrations, audit logs, SSO/SAML, and options for private control plane or VPC peering. Data residency matters for EU workloads.
[02:05] Samira: Great. quick clarifying Q: when you say 10M tokens/day, is that mixed between generation and embeddings?
[02:22] Lina: Roughly 70% generation, 30% embeddings. generation average request size 120 tokens, but some long jobs 800+ tokens for summarization.
[02:45] Daniel: Ok that matters for KV cache and memory footprint. Dedicated capacity in Redwood means a reserved GPU pool for your tenant; you get node isolation and can choose instance types. we typically recommend mixing A100‑like capacity for heavy gen and T4/RTX for embeddings depending on cost targets.
[03:12] Marcus: Is the dedicated pool single‑tenant? we need network isolation.
[03:21] Samira: Yes, Dedicated gives isolated GPU pools and we support VPC peering or private networking. for fully air‑gapped on‑prem we offer Redwood Private, but for most customers VPC with dedicated nodes meets compliance.
[03:44] Priya: How about encryption keys? we need to use our KMS/HSM.
[03:50] Daniel: We support customer‑managed keys via KMS integrations and can surface envelope encryption. audit logs are configurable and we retain request traces per your retention policy (extra retention is an add‑on).
[04:12] Lina: Burst: at month end we can see 3–4x the baseline, sometimes short spikes under 10 minutes. can you burst beyond committed capacity?
[04:27] Samira: Yes, we have burst policies: committed capacity guarantees your baseline throughput; you can purchase burst credits or allow autoscaling to spin up additional capacity in the host pool if available. there's also a cross‑region fallback option to keep SLAs.
[04:48] Daniel: technically, we keep a standby pool for burst and also allow preemptible burst nodes — those are faster and cheaper but no SLA. for strict latency SLOs you'd buy permanent nodes or reserve higher burst guarantees.
[05:12] Marcus: What's the billing model for burst? flat rate per GPU-hour?
[05:20] Samira: Bursts are billed hourly but with a premium over committed pricing; we can model blended unit economics. part of Redwood Optimize is to recommend when to use batching/caching to reduce burst needs.
[05:40] Lina: We care about latency tail. how do you handle batching vs real‑time?
[05:49] Daniel: We support dynamic batching and continuous KV cache. you can set per‑route latency SLOs and Redwood runtime will use smaller batches for lower latency routes and larger batches for throughput. caching also helps for prefix reuse in chat histories.
[06:20] Priya: For compliance, can we get isolated logs for auditors and per‑token redaction?
[06:28] Daniel: Yes, audit exports can be scoped to your tenant and redaction policies applied. we can also exclude PII fields server‑side before logs are persisted.
[06:52] Marcus: For GPU sizing — what metrics do you need from us to recommend nodes?
[06:58] Daniel: sample qps, token distribution, average and tail latency, model family you'd run (Llama‑like, Mistral, etc), and whether you need FP16/INT8 quantization.
[07:18] Lina: We're planning to run a fine‑tuned Llama‑type model for summarization and also use open‑weights for embeddings. we'd probably use a 13B model for gen; embeddings with a smaller encoder.
[07:35] Daniel: For 13B with 800 token tails, recommend A100/80GB or equivalent for efficient KV cache. for embeddings a mixed fleet with cheaper GPUs is fine. I'll dimension nodes offline and propose a mix.
[07:58] Samira: On rollouts — can you do canary and automatic fallback to hosted models if Dedicated saturates?
[08:06] Daniel: Yep, smart routing supports tiering: dedicated first, then hosted fallbacks or alternative quantized variants. that's the common pattern for reliability.
[08:24] Lina: About SLAs — what's uptime & latency guarantees?
[08:30] Samira: Dedicated comes with SLA-backed uptime targets (we'll share exact numbers in the contract) and latency SLOs we aim for but latency SLAs are usually tied to node sizing and reserved capacity.
[08:50] Marcus: What about deployment velocity — how long to provision a Dedicated pool?
[08:58] Samira: Provisioning is typically days for standard configs, but can be weeks for custom on‑prem. we can expedite for enterprise deals.
[09:12] Priya: Any regulatory controls — e.g., customer-managed audit retention, regional isolation?
[09:20] Daniel: Yes, regional node pinning, VPC peering, and private control plane in our Private offering. for most regulated customers, VPC Dedicated + KMS satisfies auditors.
[09:45] Lina: Ok let's talk cost briefly — we need a ballpark per‑token cost vs hosted.
[09:53] Samira: Dedicated reduces per‑token cost at scale compared to hosted. exact depends on utilization and batch sizes; we'll run a projection in the model Daniel produces.
[10:12] Marcus: Can we run a pilot to validate latency & cost?
[10:18] Samira: Absolutely. typical pilot: 2–4 week benchmark with representative workloads, SE runs throughput tests, we monitor token costs and latency.
[10:30] Daniel: For the pilot we need your sample traffic, keys for test environment, and acceptance criteria — e.g., p99 < 250ms and cost < $X/token.
[10:46] Priya: We'll need to validate SSO and KMS in staging. also request security question: who has access to raw requests in Redwood?
[10:58] Daniel: Access is RBAC controlled; by default only tenant admins and Redwood support with escalations can see raw payloads. we can restrict support access and require just‑in‑time access with audit trails.
[11:20] Lina: any gotchas with quantization and accuracy? we don't want quality regressions.
[11:27] Daniel: We recommend evals on your prompt set; Redwood Optimize can run automated regression checks when switching quantization or model variants. we'll include that in pilot scope.
[11:50] Samira: Recapping action items and timeline. we'll send pricing, security docs, and Daniel will size the fleet. pilot scheduling once Priya shares sample data.
[12:05] Marcus: Sounds good. can you also include a sample SLA and example contract language about dedicated capacity?
[12:12] Samira: Yes I'll include sample SLA and contract terms.
[12:20] Lina: timeline: we want to decide by end of month.
[12:24] Samira: Understood — we'll target delivering materials this week.
[12:35] --- (background chatter and a quick screen share link note) ---
[30:00] Daniel: (explaining a slide) here is a typical recommended mix: 4 A100 nodes for gen baseline, 6 cheaper GPUs for embeddings, plus a 20% burst buffer. that gives p99 headroom for your 3–4x spikes but we'll refine with your exact qps.
[31:18] Marcus: How do upgrades work if we need more nodes mid‑contract?
[31:25] Samira: You can increase committed capacity via amendment; autoscaling can also temporarily add nodes. billing proration applies.
[32:10] Priya: Are there any SOC2 gaps we should be aware of?
[32:16] Daniel: We'll share our SOC2 report. for on‑prem specific controls we may need additional support.
[33:05] Lina: Ok last question: can Redwood dedicate GPUs in EU region and keep data residency for EU requests?
[33:13] Samira: Yes we can region‑pin nodes; we offer EU region Dedicated and private control plane options to keep data local.
[33:35] Marcus: Perfect.
[34:02] Samira: Next steps recap: Samira send pricing + SLA + contract examples; Daniel run sizing + throughput projection; Priya send sample data and compliance notes; schedule pilot the week after next.
[34:20] Lina: Thanks everyone, we'll look out for the docs.
[34:26] Priya: Thanks.
[34:30] Samira: Thanks all. bye.
[41:45] (call ends)
